newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: No buyers for Manila T-bills ahead of auction.
newsitem.headline: No buyers for Manila T-bills ahead of auction.

text.p: Philippine banks raised their bid and offer quotes for Treasury bills ahead of the auction but still found no buyers in the secondary market, traders said.
"They want to see first the results of the auction later today," a foreign bank dealer said.
T-bill rates are expected to increase after the Central Bank raised its key overnight borrowing rate by 2.25 percentage points late last week.
The Central Bank had to lift its rate to quell speculation arising from the problems of the Thai baht.
Traders said T-bill rates may rise at least 30 basis points but the increase may be tempered by the high liquidity in the system.
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave offer rates of 10.375/10.90 percent for the three-month bills; 10.875/11.25 percent for the six months; and 11.125/11.60 for the one-year bills.

Meanwhile, the average interbank call loan rate rose slightly to 15.0625 percent from 15.03125 percent due to the effect of the Central Bank's heavy dollar sales on Thursday which effectively drained the market of some pesos, traders said.
"But the market was still very liquid inspite of that," a dealer said.
Done rates were from 15.25 percent to 15.03125 percent, with volume lower at 20.92 billion pesos from 21.25 billion pesos. The market had 32 lenders and 20 borrowers.
